source: Issue 665 (parent 656). The lint is test/voice-lint.lib.mjs, held by test/voice-lint.test.mjs. See docs/brand/voice.md.

notes: A string is classified by the object key or the element or attribute it is used in. A string that is classified nowhere gets the term, preferred and filler rules, but not the length limits.
label: a key whose last word is label or placeholder (label, stateLabel, aria-label, placeholder); the text of a button or label element.
title: a key whose last word is title or heading (title, heading); the text of an h1, h2 or h3 element; the title attribute.
support: a key whose last word is sub, body, description, hint or message.
The last word of a key is read after splitting camelCase and hyphens, so stateLabel is a label and aria-label is a label.

The key wins over the element. In a JavaScript call el('tag', attrs, children), the element is the last el('tag' written before the literal on the same line; a call that spans lines is not classified by its element.

Case-insensitive, whole words, accent-aware: the characters either side of a match must be neither a Unicode letter, a digit nor an underscore, so ops does not match inside copos and incrível matches Incrível.

Exact words only. No stems and no inflections: the forbidden term aguarde does not match aguardando, and the preferred term acessar does not match acesse or acessa. Add an inflection to the list when it is wanted.
A phrase matches with any run of white space between its words.
A template literal is read with each interpolation replaced by {}; {} counts as one word.
Emoji is a character with the Emoji_Presentation property, or an Extended_Pictographic one followed by U+FE0F. Text symbols without it (the status glyphs, arrows, checks) are not emoji.
A sentence ends at . ! ? or an ellipsis followed by white space and an upper case letter, or at the end of the text.

Linted: the string literals of packages/nucleo/ui/*.js and packages/nucleo/ui/screens/*.js, and the text, aria-label, placeholder and title attributes of packages/nucleo/ui/index.html. The screens are in scope because most of the text a person reads is written there.

A string literal is on-screen text only when it passes the heuristic below. Everything else is skipped: CSS class lists, ids, URLs and API paths, selectors, keys, import specifiers, event names, strings with no letter, and the operands of a comparison.

Heuristic. Skip a string with no letter; one that starts with /, ., #, http, data: or a scheme; one written after ===, !==, == or != or case; one inside console.*, import, require, querySelector, classList, getAttribute, setAttribute, addEventListener or dispatchEvent calls on its line; one with no white space that is not a single capitalised word of letters (Fechar passes, fechar, app-update and a.b do not); and one with white space whose every token is lower case ASCII with no accent and that is not classified by a key or element (a class list such as card active). A string classified as a label, title or support text skips the single-word and class-list checks, but never the URL, path and operand checks.
The rules hold new and changed code. What already broke them is frozen in test/voice-lint.baseline.json, keyed by file, rule and text (no line numbers), with a count.

The test fails on a finding that is not in the baseline and on a baseline entry that no longer occurs, so the baseline only shrinks. Never add an entry: fix the text. VOICE_LINT_SHRINK=1 rewrites the baseline with the stale entries removed.
